transcript.text: I've just bought an AEG L7FEE865R and the Eco 40-60 wash says 3:39 and seems to take forever. My old machine did a 40 wash in an hour. Is it faulty? Should I send it back?

Almost certainly not faulty: a 3:39 run time on Eco 40-60 is normal for this kind of programme, so on what you've described there's no reason to send it back. Returning it would only make sense if it shows a genuine fault, such as the cycle never finishing or an error code appearing. This sounds like normal behaviour rather than a fault: Eco 40-60 and cotton eco programmes routinely run 3-4 hours; they save energy by washing cooler for longer. The displayed time also adjusts during the cycle as the machine weighs the load and checks foam and balance. It would be worth a closer look if the cycle never finishes, the display counts down then resets repeatedly, or a code appears. To check properly, run a 60°C cottons programme (not eco or quick) with a normal load, and take the washing out as soon as it finishes. Does the washing come out warm, or still cold?
I haven't tried a 60 wash yet. On the Eco 40-60 the water barely feels warm if I touch the door, and the clothes do come out clean. Cottons 40 shows about 2 hours. Should I run the 60 as a test?

Yes, a Cottons 60 is a fair test, because it's set to heat properly, whereas Eco 40-60 is designed to run long and at a lower temperature to save energy, so a long time and a barely warm door are normal on it. With clean clothes and a normal 2-hour Cottons 40, nothing so far points to a fault. Next: Establish it should genuinely be heating (programme/temperature; not just cold rinses) before suspecting the heater. Let me know what you find.

Ok, I'll run a Cottons 60 as a test. I should say the manual lists Eco 40-60 as the longest programme, around 3.5 hours plus for a full load, so it does look like that's expected. Is there anything else I should check, or is it fine?
Next: Confirm it fills to the correct level and actually reaches the heating stage. Let me know what you find.
Ok, I'll run the Cottons 60 and let you know. I'm not sure how to check the fill level myself, though. Is there anything specific I should look for?

You can only really see it through the door glass while it washes. On a modern machine like this the water often sits just at the bottom of the drum or is barely visible, which is normal because it uses little water. Next: If there is a serious burning smell, melted insulation or smoke, stop using the machine. Let me know what you find.
Ok, thanks. No burning smell or smoke, it's been quiet and fine. I'll run the Cottons 60 and report back. Also, there's a TimeManager button I haven't used, would that be relevant?

Yes, on AEG machines TimeManager is the button that shortens (or lengthens) a programme's duration, so it is the intended way to get a quicker wash. Whether it works on Eco 40-60 depends on your model, so your manual's programme table will show which programmes accept it. Next: On a front-entry-heater design with a physically damaged heater, inspect the heater support/bracket and find why it was damaged. Let me know what you find.

Thanks. I don't think my machine has a damaged heater though, it all works fine. I'll check the manual's programme table for whether TimeManager works on Eco 40-60. Is there anything else I need to do, or is this just normal?
What makes you think it isn't heating - does the programme finish normally but the washing seems cold, or does it stop / take much longer / show an error?

I don't think it isn't heating, sorry if I gave that impression. The programme finishes and spins fine, no error codes, and the clothes come out clean. It's just the door only feels barely lukewarm on Eco 40-60 and it takes 3:39. Is that all normal?

Yes, that sounds normal: your manual lists Eco 40-60 as the longest programme at around 3. 5 hours or more for a full load, so 3:39 is in line with it. Could you tell me a bit more about what it is doing, and when it happens?
